title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Caracal: A GPU-Resident Sparse LU Solver with Lightweight Fine-Grained Scheduling
problem: Reproducibility of HPC systems research requires independent verification of claims and results. The Caracal paper claims significant speedups over existing sparse solvers.
motivation: SC25 Reproducibility Initiative aims to evaluate computational artifacts and verify research claims. This report documents independent evaluation of Caracal's implementation and performance results.
method: We independently tested Caracal, a GPU-resident sparse LU solver that uses lightweight fine-grained scheduling, following SC25's artifact evaluation guidelines. We ran the implementation, reproduced the reported results, and verified whether the claimed speedups over existing solvers actually matched the original claims.
key_novelty: Independent testing to verify that Caracal's claimed performance improvements for solving sparse linear systems on GPUs actually work.
contributions: Independent artifact evaluation of Caracal implementation
Verification of reported performance results and speedups
Documentation of evaluation methodology and findings
limitations: Reproducibility report only; full technical details in original Caracal paper (sc-2025-286).
